correctness.rationale: Rank-one projector products have squared Frobenius norm equal to overlap squared per label switch. SS, RR, FF have exact switch counts and IID has a binomial number of pair selections; conditioning yields the four finite losses and Jensen proves all ordering inequalities. A monotone Riemann error O(1/N), Laplace rescaling and domination prove the Gamma(beta+1)/(2(kt)^beta) limits whenever t^beta/N -> 0. The standalone code passed 414 checks; the infinite argument does not depend on those tests.

value.rationale: Power-law spectral shuffling advantages are a current motivated question. The theorem supplies a benchmark for all four sampling choices with an exact finite-N,t transition, including previously unavailable random-reshuffling constants and a non-universal spectral exponent dependence; these quantitative differences cannot be inferred from the marginal spectral CDF alone. The simple pair geometry is a device for discovering precise constants, not the sole claimed achievement.
